**Merge keeps both paths. Rebase makes one straight line.**

Merge adds one new commit that ties the two branches together. Your old commits keep their IDs.

Rebase copies your commits onto the tip of the other branch. The copies get new IDs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph merge
    A[main] --> M[merge commit]
    B[your work] --> M
  end
  subgraph rebase
    C[main] --> D[your work, copied] --> E[copied]
  end
```

Reach for rebase to freshen your own branch off `main` before you share it. Reach for merge to land a finished branch, and any time someone else already has your commits.

The one hard rule: never rebase commits another person has pulled. Their copies and yours stop matching.

Merge asks about conflicts once. Rebase can ask again on every commit it replays.
